positions.name: CalibrationVerificationRecord
positions.frame: what establishes that an instrument's calibration is settled — narrative confirmation and structured field-record together, and how do they relate?
positions.why: All three expressions converge on the same directional read across the dimensional passes: flat technical register with no performance (FlatTechnicalLogbook), present/realis/concrete temporal grounding, authority-ranking relational stance ratifying the instrument's readiness, expert/informational power grounded in method rather than rank, and a competence-value appeal to verification against named reference plates. src-1 delivers this as connected prose ('is now calibrated', 'We verified'), while src-2 and src-3 compress the same facts into structured field labels under a split footing (Xena animating/authoring, Quill as principal) — same claim, two formats. The conviction read is uniform 'claim' level across all three: unhedged but not ratified into decision. The set holds together as one true-because-of-what-it-describes account of the calibration's verified status, narrated two ways rather than as separate assertions.

placements.why: The document is a single-envelope calibration report for the Kestrelwood spectrograph: a settled-frequency figure ratified against named June reference plates, delivered in flat technical register (FlatTechnicalLogbook) with present/realis/concrete temporal grounding and authority-ranking, expert-power, competence-value signatures throughout. Nothing in the existing strata (empty for this repo) or graph structure covers instrument-calibration record-keeping as an organizational category, and this is exactly the kind of subject — verified instrument readiness — that future calibration envelopes across other instruments would keep feeding. No close-but-not-exact existing name exists to justify INSPIRED lineage, so this is a standalone NEW mint with no forced parent, matching the taxonomy's own named 'Calibration' category.
placements.title: Instrument and process calibration status as an organizational record category
placements.frame: Does this content document an instrument's or process's calibration, verification, or readiness state against a named standard?

placements.title: Calibration status becomes settled fact once verified against a named reference standard
placements.frame: Does this expression ground an instrument's or process's calibration status in verification against a named, checkable reference (plates, prior baselines, benchmarks) rather than asserting readiness unsupported?
placements.why: src-1's prose ('is now calibrated at 88.4 MHz... verified the calibration against the June reference plates... it holds across the full observing band') and src-2/src-3's structured field-record compression of the same facts both perform one theme: an instrument's calibration is not merely asserted but settled by grounding it in a named, checkable reference standard. This passes the narrative grain test — it names a recurring subject (how calibration claims get established as fact) that future calibration envelopes for other instruments or re-verifications would keep feeding, not a one-time measurement itself (the 88.4 MHz figure and the June-plates reference are the position-grain evidence supporting this leaf, not leaves in themselves). The uniform directional reads — flat technical register with no performance, present/realis/concrete temporal grounding, authority-ranking relational stance, expert/informational power via method, competence-value appeal, and 'claim'-level conviction across all three segments — converge on this single theme rather than three separate ones, matching the position pass's own grouping of src-1/2/3 as one account narrated two ways. No existing leaf or strata (both empty for this repo) plausibly holds this theme, and nothing close enough exists to warrant INSPIRED lineage, so this mints standalone under the newly minted Calibration strata.
